context: The scene is set at the party camp where a celebration has been soured by a private, violent confrontation: Komira is a grieving parent whose daughter Arabella died after disturbing a viper nest, and she blames Kagha (referred to in the synopsis as Sagha), the druid leader, for the death. Off-screen Komira has already drugged or tainted a cup of wine and left Kagha incapacitated at her feet, threatening to make her suffer or kill her; the rest of the party and companions are present and can step in. Depending on prior choices Kagha may be sincerely remorseful and begging for forgiveness, or cold and unrepentant and defiant, which influences how others react. The immediate moral choice for the player and companions is whether to stop Komira and spare Kagha or allow Komira to take vengeance.
